The "courses" were not academic classes at all—they were the food courses (dishes) for a University of Hong Kong residential-hall celebration, a hall dinner. The student was involved in choosing/ordering the dishes and had to submit the menu choices before a reservation deadline, just as one registers for classes. At the hall dinner—a single-evening event—the multi-course meal was served in sequence, and the student and the other guests ate the dishes, so by the end of that one evening all of the "courses" were gone. Nothing was lost, stolen, cancelled, or glitched: the student ate some of the food himself and suffered no misfortune. The puzzle only sounded like a course-registration disaster because "choosing courses before the deadline" and "all my courses were gone" also describe picking dishes for a dinner that is eaten in one night.

The "courses" were not academic classes but the food courses—the dishes—of a University of Hong Kong high-table hall dinner, a celebration held on one evening. Because the dinner required guests to choose their dishes in advance, the student had to pick his courses (his meal) before an RSVP/order deadline, which sounded exactly like registering for academic courses. At the dinner the multi-course meal was served in sequence, and the student—along with the other guests—ate the dishes; the student ate some himself and had no mishap. So by the end of that single evening all of "his courses" had been eaten, i.e., they were "gone." Nothing was lost, cancelled, stolen, glitched, or otherwise a course-selection disaster; the only trick is that "choosing courses before the deadline" and "all my courses were gone in one evening" here refer to picking and then eating dinner dishes at a hall dinner.

The "courses" were not academic classes but the food courses—the dishes—of a University of Hong Kong residential-hall high-table dinner, a one-evening celebration. Before the dinner there was a deadline by which the student had to choose his dishes (his meal courses for the dinner), which made the situation sound exactly like registering for university courses. At the dinner the meal was served course by course (a multi-course menu in sequence), and the student, along with the other attending guests at their own places, ate the dishes. The student ate some of what he had chosen but could not finish it all; the remaining courses he had selected were thrown away/discarded once the single-evening dinner ended. So by the end of that evening all of "his courses" were gone—some eaten, the rest discarded—with no theft, system glitch, cancellation, or lost reservation. The only trick is linguistic: "choosing courses before the deadline" and "all my courses were gone in one evening" refer here to picking and then consuming (and discarding the leftovers of) dinner dishes at a hall high-table dinner, not to a course-registration disaster.
